newsitem.title: USA: Calif. budget talks resume ahead of July deadline.
newsitem.headline: Calif. budget talks resume ahead of July deadline.

text.p: California lawmakers resumed their budget talks on Monday, but officials held out little hope that a spending plan would be enacted before the start of the 1997-1998 fiscal year on July 1.
The legislature's budget conference committee -- made up of three senators and three assembly members -- has been holding daily hearings on the state's key fiscal issues.
The committee's goal is to meld the budget packages of the state Assembly and Senate into a single spending plan for the fiscal year that begins July 1.
The conference committee has already missed the state's Constitutional budget deadline of June 15.

Senate President Bill Lockyer, a Democrat, told legislators that the budget committee was unlikely to conclude its deliberations before next week, giving the Senate and Assembly little time to act before the July 1 deadline.
